name: Cuiabano Portuguese
notes: The traditional speech of the Cuiabá river valley (Baixada Cuiabana), Mato Grosso, as described by Almeida (2004) for riverside speakers with little schooling, about fifty years old, of Cuiabá-born parents (p. 149). /t d/ stay stops before [i] (pp. 151-152). ⟨ch x j⟩ and soft ⟨g⟩ are commonly the affricates [t͡ʃ d͡ʒ] (pp. 154-155). Coda /S/ is palato-alveolar, mainly word-finally (p. 153). Coda /l/ and coda /R/ are retroflex (pp. 157, 159). Onset strong /R/ is a trill (pp. 158-159), and word-final /R/ tends to drop (p. 159). Each of these alternates with the pt-BR form, even in one speaker; the spec gives the traditional form first. The ALiB rates /t d/ palatalisation in the capital as 'moderada' (Battisti & Dornelles Filho 2015: 226).

allophone_rules.notes: DISABLED: /t/ stays a stop before [i]; see the positional before_i map.
DISABLED: /d/ stays a stop before [i]; see the positional before_i map.

Onset /ʃ/ (⟨ch x⟩) is the affricate [t͡ʃ]. Almeida (2004: 154-155): the fricatives 'comumente são pronunciadas, respectivamente, como africadas surda /tS/ e sonora /dZ/': [tSe»ga] chegar, [»petSi] peixe, [»putSa] puxa.
Onset /ʒ/ (⟨j⟩, soft ⟨g⟩) is the affricate [d͡ʒ]. Almeida (2004: 155): [»dZe)ti] gente, [»dZa] já, [»odZi] hoje.

Coda /S/ is palato-alveolar [ʃ]. Almeida (2004: 153): alveolar /s/ 'passa a pré-palatal /S/, principalmente quando se encontra em final de vocábulo: [»doS] dois, [»maS] mas', and also word-internally: [»fEStaS] festas.
Voiced counterpart of CUIABA_CODA_S. Almeida (2004: 154): 'O recuo do ponto de articulação também ocorre com a sonora [z] > [Z]'.

The palatal coda /S/ takes the voicing of a following voiced consonant: mesmo [ˈmeʒmu], rasga [ˈraʒɡɐ]. Almeida (2004: 154): 'O recuo do ponto de articulação também ocorre com a sonora [z] > [Z]', with [»raZga] rasga and [»vaZa] várzea. The rule runs in the second pass, after CUIABA_CODA_S has written the coda as [ʃ].

Word-final /R/ drops: 'Quando temos /R/ em final de vocábulo, a tendência é ocorrer o apagamento da consoante: [fa»ze] fazer, [ka»za] casar, [mu»¥E] mulher' (Almeida 2004: 159). The rate is below 100 %, and slow speech keeps a retroflex.

An ⟨r⟩ after a coda consonant is the strong rhotic, the trill of rapaz and burro (Almeida 2004: 158-159): honra [ˈõrɐ], genro [ˈd͡ʒẽru]. Cristófaro Silva (2025: 240) puts the R-forte in one class across three contexts: 'início de sílaba que coincide com início de palavra (rapaz, rio, rosa etc.); início de sílaba em meio de palavra (carro, terra) ou início de sílaba após consoante (Israel, desrespeito etc.)'.

location.notes: Cuiabá — the centre of the Baixada Cuiabana, the river valley this spec models. [Wikidata Q170762 P625]
